Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:10:1.hebrew: נתינה נתינה - כתיב הכא ״תתן לו״, וכתיב התם בנזקי עבד ״כסף שלשים שקלים יתן לאדוניו״ (שם כא):
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:10:1.english: "Giving" "giving" - It is written here, "you shall give to him," and it is written there, regarding damages [caused by an ox to] a slave, "thirty shekels of silver he shall give to his master" (Exodus 21).

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:12:1.hebrew: ונילף נתינה נתינה מעבד חדא דתפשתה מרובה כו' - כולה חדא קושיא היא, עד "עבד מעבד הוה ליה למילף":
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:12:1.english: And let us derive "giving" "giving" from a slave; one, that if you grasped too much etc. - All of it is one single question, up to "he should have derived a slave from a slave."

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:14:1.hebrew: מיכה מיכה גמר - אין אדם דן ג"ש מעצמו, ומסורה היא להם מרבותיהם ומסיני, איזו תיבה נכתבה לג"ש, ככל דבר הלמד מחבירו. ועד השתא דהוה אמרינן דרבי שמעון גמר מרביה דנתינת הענק נדרש לג"ש, הוה פרכינן: ג"ש מנא ליה? דגמר מנתינה דערכין, נגמר מנתינה דעבד! מש"ה איצטריך לתרוצי: ג"ש דר' שמעון לאו ג"ש דנתינה גמר, אלא דמיכה. כתיב בעבד (ויקרא כ״ה:ל״ט) וכי ימוך, וכתיב בערכין (שם כז) ואם מך הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:14:1.english: He derives "poverty" from "poverty" - A person does not derive a verbal analogy on their own; rather, it is a tradition they received from their teachers, going back to Sinai, as to which word was written for the purpose of a verbal analogy, like any matter that is learned from its fellow. Until now, since we were saying that Rabbi Shimon derived it from his teacher, that the "giving" of the parting gift is expounded as a verbal analogy, we were objecting: From where does he have this verbal analogy? That he derives it from the "giving" of valuations, [so] let him derive it from the "giving" of a slave! Therefore it was necessary to answer: Rabbi Shimon's verbal analogy is not derived from "giving", but from "poverty". It is written regarding a slave (Leviticus 25:39), "And if your brother grows poor," and it is written regarding valuations (ibid. 27:8), "But if he is too poor."

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:15:1.hebrew: היינו דכתיב צאן גורן ויקב - למימר שדי ג"ש אכל חד מינייהו, דהוו להו ט"ו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:15:1.english: This is [the reason] that it is written “flock, threshing floor, and winepress” - To say: Cast a gezerah shavah (verbal analogy) on each one of them, so that they amount to fifteen [sela].

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:15:2.hebrew: למה לי - הואיל וסופו לרבות כל דבר מאשר ברכך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:15:2.english: Why do I need [it]? - Since its end includes any item, from “with which the Lord your God has blessed you”:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:16:1.hebrew: בכלל ברכה - צאן פרה ורבה, וכן גידולי קרקע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:16:1.english: Included in the category of blessing - Flocks are fruitful and multiply, and so too are the produce of the ground.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:1:1.hebrew: (יכול אפילו חלה - בתוך שש יהא חייב להשלים ימי חליו:)
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:1:1.english: (One might have thought: even if he became ill - within the six [years], he would be obligated to make up the days of his illness.)

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:1:2.hebrew: (ת"ל ובשביעית יצא. ואפילו לא עבד שש שלימים:)
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:1:2.english: (The verse states: "And in the seventh he shall go out." [This means he goes out] even if he did not work six full [years].)

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:2:1.hebrew: ופגע בו יובל - אחרי כן, למחרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:2:1.english: And the Jubilee arrived - Afterward, on the next day.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:3:1.hebrew: בעושה מעשה מחט - בחליו, שהוא מעשה קל. קתני לעיל "כל שש" אינו חייב להשלים, דהא עבד ליה מלאכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:3:1.english: Where he performs needlework - During his illness, which is a light task. [The baraita] taught above that [if he was sick] "all six" [years] he is not obligated to complete [the time], since he did perform work for him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:4:1.hebrew: חלה ד' נעשה כו' - דהכי קתני: כי חלה שלש, אינו משלים; חלה יותר מכאן, כחלה כל שש, והוא חייב להשלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:4:1.english: If he was sick for four, he becomes etc. - For this is what [the baraita] teaches: When he was sick for three, he does not complete [the service]; if he was sick more than this, [it is] like one who was sick for all six, and he is obligated to complete [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:1.hebrew: מכל מין ומין - מצאנך ומגרנך ומיקבך, שוה ה' סלעים מכל אחד, שהן ט"ו סלעים. ולקמיה פריך: מנינא אתא לאשמועינן?
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:1.english: Of each and every type - From your flock, and from your threshing floor, and from your winepress, [he gives] the value of five sela from each one, which is fifteen sela. And later [the Gemara] asks: Did [the verse] come to teach us [only] a number?

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:2.hebrew: כשלשים של עבד - נזק שור מועד שהרג את העבד, ולקמיה יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:2.english: Like the thirty of a slave - The damages [paid by the owner of] a forewarned ox that killed a slave; and later [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:3.hebrew: כחמשים של ערכין - הוא ערך גדול שבערכין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:5:3.english: Like the fifty of valuations - This is the largest valuation among the valuations.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:6:1.hebrew: מנינא אתא לאשמועינן - בשלשה מינין של חמש הוו להו ט"ו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:6:1.english: Did he come to teach us a count? - With three types of five, they are fifteen.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:6:2.hebrew: הא קמ"ל כו' - להכי תני שהן חמש עשרה, לאשמועינן דלא קפיד אלא אמנינא דט"ו סלעים, אבל אחמש מכל מין לא קפיד. דאי בציר ליה מהאי וטפי ליה מהאי, לית לן בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:6:2.english: This it teaches us, etc. - For this reason it taught "which are fifteen": to teach us that he is particular only about the number of fifteen sela, but he is not particular about five of each type. For if he gives less of this one and more of that one, we have no problem with it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:7:1.hebrew: ריקם ריקם - לא תשלחנו ריקם (דברים ט״ו:י״ג), ובפדיון הבן כתיב (שמות ל״ד:כ׳) "וכל בכור בניך תפדה ולא יראו פני ריקם":
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:7:1.english: “Empty,” “empty” - “You shall not send him away empty” (Deuteronomy 15:13); and with regard to the redemption of the son it is written (Exodus 34:20), “And all the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and none shall appear before Me empty.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:8:1.hebrew: אי כתיב ריקם לבסוף - "הענק תעניק לו מצאנך מגרנך מיקבך", ו"לא תשלחנו ריקם" היה כתוב אחריהם, כדקאמרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:8:1.english: If “empty” were written at the end - “You shall surely furnish him from your flock, from your threshing floor, and from your winepress,” and “you shall not send him away empty” were written after them, as you say.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:8:2.hebrew: ריקם מעיקרא - כתוב קודם "הענק תעניק", ולכן שדי "ריקם" על כל אחד כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:8:2.english: “Empty” at the outset - It is written before “you shall surely furnish” (Deut. 15:14), and therefore cast [the word] “empty” onto each one, etc.:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:9:1.hebrew: מעולת ראיה - דליתיה אלא שתי כסף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:9:1.english: From the burnt-offering of appearance - For it is only [worth] two silver [coins].

Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:9:2.hebrew: אשר ברכך - סיפא דהענק תעניק הוא, ללמדך שתדרוש המקרא לרבות ולא למעט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17a:9:2.english: Of that with which He has blessed you - This is the latter part of [the verse] “you shall surely furnish him” (ha'anek ta'anik), to teach you that you should expound the verse to include [more] and not to limit.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:12:1.hebrew: חדא דתפשתה מרובה לא תפשתה - תימה: כיון דכתיב "אשר ברכך", הוה לן למילף מן המרובה, כדאמר לעיל דפריך: "ונילף ריקם ריקם מעולת ראיה?", ומשני: אמר קרא "אשר ברכך". וי"ל דלא דמי; דלעיל לא כתב אלא חד ריקם אבכור ועולת ראיה, אית לן למילף מן המרובה משום "אשר ברכך". אבל הכא, חד נתינה כתיב גבי עבד, וחד גבי ערכין, ואין לומר דאשר ברכך קאי אמרובה, דהיינו ערכין, אם סברא ללמד מעבד, משום דתפשת מועט תפשת. ותדע, דהא כי יליף מערכין, מהני "אשר ברכך" לאפוקי דלא נילף מפחות שבערכין, כדפריך בסמוך: "ונילף מפחות שבערכין?", ומשני: אמר קרא "אשר ברכך":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:12:1.english: One [answer is that] if you grasped too much, you did not grasp - It is astonishing: since it is written "with which the Lord your God has blessed you," we should have derived from the larger amount, as [the Gemara] said above, where it asks: "Let us derive [the law of] 'empty-handed, empty-handed' from the burnt offering of appearance?", and answers: The verse says "with which He has blessed you." And one can answer that they are not alike; for above, only one instance of "empty-handed" is written, regarding the firstborn and the burnt offering of appearance, so we must derive from the larger one because of "with which He has blessed you." But here, one [instance of] giving is written regarding a slave, and one regarding valuations. And one cannot say that "with which He has blessed you" refers to the larger one, namely valuations, if it is reasonable to derive from the slave, because "if you grasped a bit, you grasped." And know [that this is so], for when [the Gemara] derives from valuations, "with which He has blessed you" serves to exclude deriving from the lowest of the valuations, as [the Gemara] asks shortly after: "Let us derive from the lowest of the valuations?", and answers: The verse says "with which He has blessed you."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:3:1.hebrew: חלה שלש ועבד שלש אינו חייב להשלים - יש שהיו רוצים לומר שאותם שכירים מלמדי תינוקות, אם חלו חצי זמן, כמו כן לא יהיו משלימים את זמנן כמו ע"ע דהכא, ויטלו כל השכירות כיון שהיו אנוסין. וקשה, דבפרק השוכר את האומנין (ב"מ דף עז.) קאמר רב: פועל יכול לחזור בו, ואפילו בחצי היום. ופריך: והתנן, השוכר את הפועל ושמע שמת לו מת, או שאחזתו חמה, יכול לחזור בו. טעמא דמת לו מת שאנוס הוא, הא לאו הכי אינו יכול לחזור בו. והשתא, אי היכא דאניס נוטל שכירותו משלם, מאי פריך לרב? דילמא היכא דמת לו מת דאניס הוא נוטל שכירות משלם, ורב איירי בדלא אניס, ואינו נוטל אלא מה שהרויח! אלא ע"כ אף כי נמי הוי אנוס אינו נוטל אלא מה שהרויח, ואי לא אניס ידו על התחתונה, דבעה"ב שוכר עליו אם באתה חבילתו לידו או מטעהו, כדאמר (שם עה:) גבי השוכר את הפועל להעלות פשתנו מן המשרה. והשתא פריך שפיר לרב. וא"כ מלמדי תינוקות נמי, אם חלו לא יקחו אלא מה שהרויחו, דאין לדמותם כלל לע"ע, דעבד עברי גופו קנוי לאדונו. הילכך חלה שלש אינו חייב להשלים, דאין יכול לעשות מלאכה יותר מיכולתו. אבל מלמד אין גופו קנוי, אלא שכר עצמו ללמוד עד הזמן, וכשאינו יכול להשלים לא יטול אלא מה שהרויח. ועוד נראה לחלק בין מלמד לע"ע דעבד: היכא דחלה ג' ועבד ג', היינו טעמא דאינו חייב להשלים, משום דכתיב בספר (ישעיהו ט״ז:י״ד): "מקצה שלש שנים כשני שכיר", אם כן מצינו דשנים דשכיר הן שלש שנים, והיינו דכתיב: "כי משנה שכר שכיר עבדך שש שנים". והילכך היכא דעבד שלש, דהיינו שני שכיר, אמר דאינו חייב להשלים ויטול שכרו, כיון דעבדו ג' שנים דהיינו שני שכיר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:3:1.english: If he was sick for three [years] and worked for three, he is not obligated to complete - Some wanted to say that those hired teachers of children, if they were sick for half the term, likewise would not have to complete their term, like the Hebrew slave here, and they would receive the entire wage, since they were prevented by circumstances beyond their control. But this is difficult, for in the chapter "HaSocher et HaUmanin" (Bava Metzia 77a) Rav says: A laborer may retract, even in the middle of the day. And [the Gemara] challenges: But we learned in a mishnah: One who hires a laborer, and [the laborer] heard that a relative of his died, or that he was seized by a heat-stroke, may retract. The reason is that a relative of his died, for he is under duress; but otherwise, he could not retract. Now, if where he is under duress he receives his full wage, what is the challenge to Rav? Perhaps where a relative of his died, since he is under duress, he receives his full wage, and Rav is speaking about a case where he is not under duress, and he receives only what he earned! Rather, one must say that even when he is under duress, he receives only what he earned, and if he is not under duress, his hand is on the bottom [i.e., he is at a disadvantage], since the employer hired him [with the concern] whether his bundle will come into his hand or whether [the laborer] will mislead him, as it says (ibid. 75b) regarding one who hires a laborer to bring up his flax from the steeping pool. And now the challenge to Rav is well founded. And if so, teachers of children too, if they fell ill, will receive only what they earned, for they cannot be compared at all to a Hebrew slave, as a Hebrew slave's body is acquired by his master. Therefore, if he was sick for three [years] he is not obligated to complete, since he cannot do work beyond his ability. But a teacher's body is not acquired; rather he hired himself out to teach until the [end of the] term, and when he cannot complete it, he receives only what he earned. And furthermore, it appears to distinguish between a teacher and a Hebrew slave: Where he was sick for three [years] and worked for three, the reason that he is not obligated to complete is because it is written in the book of (Isaiah 16:14): "Within three years, like the years of a hired worker," so we find that "the years of a hired worker" are three years, and this is what is written: "For he has served you for double the hire of a hired worker, six years." Therefore, where he worked three [years], which are the years of a hired worker, [Scripture] says that he is not obligated to complete and he takes his wages, since he worked three years, which are the years of a hired worker:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:9:1.hebrew: ונילף ריקם ריקם מעולת ראיה - וא"ת: בעולת ראיה גופה מנא לן דבכל שהוא? נילף מבכור, ותהא ה' סלעים! וי"ל: דשמא הלכה למשה מסיני הוא דבכל שהוא. דהא למ"ד בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף ז.) דעולת ראיה שתי כסף דבר תורה — אמרו בירושלמי פ"ק דמסכת פאה דהוי הלכה למשה מסיני:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17a:9:1.english: "And let us derive 'empty' 'empty' from the burnt-offering of appearance" - And if you ask: With regard to the burnt-offering of appearance itself, from where do we know that [it may be brought] with any amount? Let us derive [it] from the firstborn, and it should be five sela! And one can answer: Perhaps it is a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai that [it may be] with any amount. For according to the one who says in the first chapter of Chagigah (7a) that the burnt-offering of appearance is [a minimum of] two kesef by Torah law — [still,] they said in the Jerusalem Talmud, in the first chapter of tractate Peah, that it is a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai:
